concepts.description: Quick digit tests for 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10 and 11 that avoid long division.

concepts.name: Missing digits
concepts.description: Turn a divisibility rule into an equation for the unknown digit.

concepts.name: Composite divisors

formulas.title: The core rules
formulas.prompt: What are the divisibility tests for 3, 4, 8 and 9?
formulas.formula:
3, 9: digit sum divisible by 3 or 9
4: last two digits divisible by 4
8: last three digits divisible by 8
2, 5, 10: last digit
formulas.explanation: 10 leaves remainder 1 when divided by 3 or 9, so a number and its digit sum have the same remainder. 100 is a multiple of 4 and 1000 of 8, so only the last digits matter.
formulas.example:
7,324 → last two digits 24 ÷ 4 ✓
2,346 → digit sum 15 → divisible by 3
formulas.commonMistake: Checking the last digit only for 4 or 8.

formulas.title: Divisibility by 11
formulas.prompt: How do you test for divisibility by 11?
formulas.formula: (sum of digits in odd places) − (sum of digits in even places) = 0 or a multiple of 11
formulas.explanation: Because 10 ≡ −1 (mod 11), place values alternate between +1 and −1.
formulas.commonMistake: Adding all the digits, which is the rule for 3 and 9.

formulas.title: Composite divisors
formulas.prompt: How do you test for divisibility by 6, 12 or 24?
formulas.explanation: A number divisible by two coprime numbers is divisible by their product. Non-coprime pairs such as 2 and 6 prove nothing extra.
formulas.example: 24: divisible by 3 and 8 ✓ (but 4 and 6 is not enough)
formulas.applicationPrompt: How would you test a number for divisibility by 88?

formulas.title: Missing digit
formulas.prompt: A digit is missing from a number that must be divisible by 9. How do you find it?
formulas.formula:
Digit sum must reach the next multiple of 9
Missing digit = (9 − sum of known digits mod 9) mod 9
formulas.explanation: The known digits leave a remainder r; the missing digit must top the sum up to the next multiple of 9.
formulas.commonMistake: Answering 0 and 9 as if both worked, or forgetting the known digits.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Find the digit x so that 73x4 is divisible by 9.

formulas.title: Smallest and counting
formulas.prompt: How do you find the smallest k-digit multiple of m, or count multiples of a or b?
formulas.formula:
Smallest k-digit multiple = ⌈10^(k−1) ÷ m⌉ × m
A or B: ⌊n/a⌋ + ⌊n/b⌋ − ⌊n/LCM⌋
formulas.explanation: Round the first k-digit number up to a multiple of m. For counting, subtract the overlap once.
formulas.commonMistake: Starting with the smallest k-digit number without rounding up.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Find the smallest 4-digit number divisible by 9.

formulas.title: Test for 7
formulas.prompt: How do you test a number for divisibility by 7 without dividing?
formulas.formula:
Double the last digit and subtract it from the rest.
Repeat; the number is divisible by 7 if the result is.
formulas.explanation: The operation changes the number by a multiple of 7, so divisibility is preserved.
formulas.example: 343: 34 − 2 × 3 = 28, a multiple of 7, so 343 is divisible by 7.
formulas.commonMistake: Adding the doubled digit instead of subtracting it.

formulas.title: Multiples in a range
formulas.prompt: How many multiples of k lie from a to b inclusive?
formulas.explanation: Count the multiples up to b and remove those below a.
formulas.commonMistake: Using ⌊a/k⌋, which drops a itself when a is a multiple of k.
formulas.applicationPrompt: How many numbers from 100 to 300 are divisible by 6?

levels.title: Tests That Beat Long Division
levels.description: Read the divisibility off the digits instead of dividing.

blocks.title: Why digit tests work
blocks.body: A place value like 100 or 1000 is already a multiple of 4 or 8, so only the last digits can matter. And since 10 leaves remainder 1 when divided by 3 or 9, every place value behaves like 1: a number and its digit sum have the same remainder.

blocks.title: The core tests
blocks.body:
3, 9: digit sum
4: last two digits
8: last three digits
11: alternating digit sum
blocks.caption: 2, 5 and 10 look only at the last digit.

blocks.title: Composite divisors
blocks.body: To test divisibility by 24, test 3 and 8. Only split into coprime parts: passing the tests for 4 and 6 says nothing extra, since both share a factor of 2.

questions.question: Which of these numbers is divisible by 3?
questions.explanation: Digit sums: 1234 → 10, 2346 → 15, 4510 → 10, 5221 → 10. Only 15 is a multiple of 3.
solutionSteps: Add the digits of each number.
commonMistakes: Looking at the last digit only.

questions.question: Which of these numbers is divisible by 4?
questions.explanation: Only the last two digits matter: 14, 18, 24 and 10. Only 24 is divisible by 4.
solutionSteps: Take the last two digits of each.

hints.text: 100 is a multiple of 4, so hundreds and above never matter.

commonMistakes: Testing only the last digit (even ⇒ divisible by 4).

questions.question: What is the remainder when 1,234 is divided by 9?
questions.explanation: A number has the same remainder as its digit sum when divided by 9. 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10, and 10 ÷ 9 leaves 1.
questions.method: Remainder mod 9 = remainder of the digit sum.

questions.question: A number is divisible by 11 if

options.text: its digit sum is divisible by 11
its last two digits are divisible by 11
the difference between the sums of digits in odd and even places is 0 or a multiple of 11

questions.explanation: For 11 the digits alternate between +1 and −1 place value, so the alternating sum decides.

hints.text: The digit-sum rule is the one for 3 and 9.

commonMistakes: Using the digit sum, which is the rule for 3 and 9.

questions.question: Which of these numbers is divisible by both 2 and 9?
questions.explanation: 1134 is even and its digit sum 1 + 1 + 3 + 4 = 9 is a multiple of 9. 1135 and 2345 are odd; 1244 has digit sum 11.
commonMistakes: Checking only one of the two conditions.

questions.question: If the number 73x4 (x is a single digit) is divisible by 9, what is x?
questions.explanation: The digit sum 7 + 3 + x + 4 = 14 + x must be a multiple of 9. The next multiple of 9 after 14 is 18, so x = 4. Check: 7344 = 9 × 816.
questions.method: Top the digit sum up to the next multiple of 9.

hints.text: What is the next multiple of 9 above that sum?

commonMistakes: Making the digit sum 9 instead of 18.

questions.question: Which of these numbers is divisible by 11?
questions.explanation: Alternating sum for 2728: (2 + 2) − (7 + 8) = −11, a multiple of 11. The others give 4, −1 and 9.

hints.text: Add digits in alternate positions separately.

questions.question: Which pair of tests correctly proves that a number is divisible by 24?
questions.explanation: 24 = 3 × 8 with 3 and 8 coprime. Pairs such as 4 and 6 share the factor 2, so a number like 12 passes both tests without being divisible by 24.
solutionSteps: Counter-example for the others: 12 is divisible by 4, 6, 2, 12 but not by 24.
commonMistakes: Choosing 4 and 6 because they multiply to 24.

questions.question: What is the smallest 4-digit number divisible by 9?
questions.explanation: The smallest 4-digit number is 1000, with digit sum 1. Adding 8 makes the digit sum 9. So 1008 is the smallest. Check: 1008 = 9 × 112.
questions.method: Round the smallest k-digit number up to a multiple.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 6,573 is divided by 8?
questions.explanation: 1000 is divisible by 8, so only the last three digits matter: 573 ÷ 8 = 71 remainder 5.
questions.method: Only the last three digits affect divisibility by 8.

hints.text: Which part of the number is always a multiple of 8?

questions.question: What is the smallest 5-digit number divisible by 88?
questions.explanation: 10000 ÷ 88 ≈ 113.6, so the next whole multiple is 114 × 88 = 10032. (Check: 113 × 88 = 9944, which has only 4 digits.)
questions.method: Round the smallest k-digit number up to the next multiple.

questions.question: How many numbers from 1 to 200 are divisible by 3 or 5?

hints.text: Some numbers are counted in both lists.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 987,654 is divided by 11?
questions.explanation: Alternating sum from the right: 4 − 5 + 6 − 7 + 8 − 9 = −3. Add 11 to bring it into range: −3 + 11 = 8. Check: 11 × 89,786 = 987,646, and 987,654 − 987,646 = 8.
questions.method: The alternating sum is congruent to the remainder mod 11.

hints.text: What do you do with a negative result?
